items.title: Critical FortiMail zero-day CVE-2026-104286 under active exploitation
items.summary: Fortinet published advisory FG-IR-26-175 on Oct 1 for CVE-2026-104286, a CVSS 9.8 path-traversal + null-byte flaw in FortiMail that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files to the appliance via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests. It affects FortiMail 8.0.0-8.0.1, 7.6.0-7.6.6, 7.4.0-7.4.8 and 7.2.0-7.2.9. Fortinet confirms active exploitation; fixes (8.0.2, 7.6.7, 7.4.9) were still unreleased at disclosure, so customers on those branches must apply workarounds: disable IBE via CLI or block internet access to the management interface. 7.2 users must upgrade to the 7.4 branch or above. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 1 with an Oct 4 deadline for federal agencies. Fortinet also published IoCs (file hashes, IPs, log entries).
items.why_it_matters: This is the second actively-exploited 9.8 in two days (Cisco SD-WAN Manager yesterday). Any customer with internet-reachable FortiMail is an immediate compromise risk, and there is no full patch yet for most branches. Presales moment: offer a version/internet-exposure check and a compromise-assessment conversation for every FortiMail customer — the CISA Oct 4 deadline gives you a forcing function.

items.title: New Data Intelligence capabilities for production AI: native MCP integration, PureKVA inference acceleration
items.summary: At Accelerate London, Everpure announced new Data Intelligence capabilities shipping this October: native Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration so AI agents and security tools can query live data catalogs in natural language and get sensitivity classifications back; Privacy-First File Intelligence (who can access each share + staleness, without reading contents); Pure Key-Value Accelerator (PureKVA) on FlashBlade pre-staging KV cache directly into GPU memory for up to 20x faster time-to-first-token (vendor claim); Always-On DeepReduce continuous sub-block compression including on pre-compressed content; and an Intelligent Token Optimization reference architecture using open-weight models to cut external API token spend. Data Intelligence builds on the 1Touch acquisition and spans the Everpure platform, public clouds, SaaS and third-party storage.
items.why_it_matters: Everpure is turning storage into governed data infrastructure for agents — this is the counter to NetApp's just-announced Novus AI storage architecture. For AI-storage deals, ask who owns governed agent data access: PureKVA is FlashBlade-only (not FlashArray), and the 20x TTFT claim needs proof on the customer's own dataset. Real differentiator for agent-readiness conversations this quarter.

items.title: Analyst day: new long-term outlook, four growth vectors, FY27 reaffirmed + preliminary FY28 guide
items.summary: At its 2026 financial analyst meeting (Oct 1), Everpure outlined durable accelerated growth through four strategic vectors: core enterprise storage, hyperscaler solutions, and new data-management markets. The company reaffirmed its FY2027 outlook, gave a preliminary FY2028 outlook, and highlighted 19% of revenue consistently reinvested in R&D over five years plus eight consecutive quarters of accelerating revenue growth. CEO Charlie Giancarlo framed it as an inflection point expanding from enterprise storage into hyperscaler data management.
items.why_it_matters: Everpure is explicitly telling Wall Street it is going after hyperscaler business — a competitive escalation signal for Dell, HPE, and NetApp in large AI-infrastructure deals. Expect sharper pricing and more aggressive positioning on mega-deals; flag this when Everpure shows up in AI-data-center bids.

items.title: Amazon hikes EC2 Capacity Block GPU rental prices ~15%; reportedly offloading $8B in Nvidia chips in sale-leaseback
items.summary: Amazon announced ~15% price increases starting next week on EC2 Capacity Blocks (reserved GPU compute on Nvidia A100 through B300 chips), and the FT reports Amazon is looking to offload ~$8B of advanced Nvidia chips to outside investors and lease them back. The moves point to a hyperscaler financing crunch: Amazon plans $220B in 2026 capex and says demand still outstrips supply through 2028. Nvidia also disclosed a $150B buyback authorization (Sept 28), bringing total repurchase capacity to a record $235B.
items.why_it_matters: Hyperscaler GPU rentals just got 15% more expensive — the on-prem/private-AI TCO story gets stronger every time cloud GPU economics deteriorate. Use the sale-leaseback as evidence customers want GPU capacity without balance-sheet ownership: exactly what Dell/HPE AI-infrastructure deals offer. Good talk track for any 'why not just run it in AWS' objection.

items.title: Critical SD-WAN Manager zero-day CVE-2026-76504 actively exploited
items.summary: Cisco published advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU on Sept 30 for CVE-2026-76504, a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated API authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. A crafted HTTP request with a URI-encoded character in the j_security_check path (e.g. POST /%6a_security_check) lets a remote attacker with no credentials use the Manager API as the admin user, gaining full control of the device and the SD-WAN fabric it manages. Fixed releases are available (20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1, 26.2.1); there is no workaround. Cisco confirmed active exploitation in September, and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 1, with a remediation deadline of Oct 3 for federal civilian agencies.
items.why_it_matters: Any customer running an on-prem Catalyst SD-WAN Manager is exposed, and Internet-reachable managers are at immediate risk. This is a proactive-outreach moment: tell customers to verify their version, apply the fixed release, restrict Manager access from the public internet to trusted hosts, and check serviceproxy-access.log for encoded j_security_check requests from unknown IPs plus vmanage-server.log for j_security_check calls under viptela-reserved- usernames.

items.title: $1.2B Vultr order for AMD Helios AI racks; networking growth outlook raised
items.summary: HPE announced Sept 30 a $1.2 billion order from cloud provider Vultr for AMD Helios AI Rack systems to be deployed in Vultr's US data centers - HPE's first order for the new AMD Helios platform. Each rack combines 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs with EPYC 'Venice' CPUs and Pensando Vulcano AI NICs; HPE supplies the networking layer (six HPE Juniper Networking QFX5252 scale-up Ethernet switch trays per rack), direct liquid cooling, and deployment services. At its networking Investor Day the same day, HPE raised its long-term networking revenue CAGR to the high teens for FY26-FY29 (from 5-7%) and FY27 networking growth to high-teens/low-20s, and lifted the Juniper acquisition synergy target to $800M annual run-rate by FY28.
items.why_it_matters: The biggest public proof point that HPE's post-Juniper stack is winning neocloud AI deals against Dell and Supermicro - a citable customer win for AI-infrastructure conversations. The per-rack scale-up Ethernet design (QFX5252) is also a usable counter-position to NVIDIA InfiniBand pitches, and the raised outlook signals HPE expects AI networking budgets to stay strong into FY27.

items.title: MoU with JERA and RHAELM for $15B hyperscale AI data center in Japan
items.summary: On Oct 1, JERA (Japan's biggest power generator), Dell Technologies, and UK-based AI infrastructure developer RHAELM signed an MoU to develop a standardized, repeatable framework for building AI infrastructure at national scale in Japan, starting with a $15 billion, 400-megawatt hyperscale AI data center in Chiba. JERA will provide land next to its Chiba power station plus 400 MW of power under a 15- to 25-year agreement; RHAELM will develop, construct, operate and finance the facility (Apollo Global Management as strategic investment partner); Dell will provide standardized rack-scale AI infrastructure. Phased operation begins in 2028 with full 400 MW capacity targeted for 2029.
items.why_it_matters: National-scale sovereign-AI validation of Dell's rack-scale AI factory positioning - a strong reference-architecture talking point for large AI data-center deals. Also worth watching the financing pattern: infrastructure funds bankrolling multi-billion-dollar builds is a model more customers will ask about.

items.summary: Everpure announced a set of FlashBlade data-management capabilities aimed at production AI: native Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration so AI agents and security tools can query live data catalogs in natural language and see each dataset's sensitivity class; privacy-first file intelligence that shows who can access each share and how stale it is without ever reading file content; and turn-key deployment through the existing Pure1 console. On performance, the PureKVA Key-Value Accelerator pre-stages context directly into GPU memory for up to 20x faster time to first token with zero dataset relocation, while Always-On DeepReduce scans blocks continuously for sub-block similarities to expand usable capacity without write-performance impact or manual scheduling.
items.title: Everpure adds AI data-management capabilities to FlashBlade: native MCP, PureKVA inference acceleration, always-on DeepReduce
items.why_it_matters: Gives storage-refresh conversations a real AI story: 'AI execution at the data, without moving it.' The MCP angle is the presales hook for AI-agent projects — agents need governed access to live enterprise context, and Everpure is selling the data side of that. File-intelligence-before-AI-access is also a clean risk-reduction pitch for security-minded buyers.

items.summary: Everpure's Global Data Sovereignty Report 2026 (2,100 enterprise leaders across 8 countries) finds 88% of C-suite leaders believe a data sovereignty failure could cost them their jobs and 91% fear financial or reputational damage. Yet 64% of organizations operate with no formal sovereignty strategy, 62% lack full visibility into who can access their data, and 85% say they would compromise on features to work with a local or sovereign provider. 40% are already limiting use of SaaS providers on non-domestic infrastructure.
items.title: Everpure sovereignty survey: 88% of execs fear a sovereignty failure could cost them their jobs
items.why_it_matters: Sovereignty is now a budget-level business risk, not just a compliance checkbox. These stats are ready-made discovery material for security and regulated-industry conversations: ask where their data actually lives, who can touch it, and what the plan is for geopolitical disruption — most won't have an answer.

items.summary: CrowdStrike announced at OpenAI DevDay that the Falcon platform is available in the OpenAI Marketplace: eligible OpenAI enterprise customers can procure Falcon using a portion of their existing OpenAI commitments. The announcement extends the partnership around securing the 'agentic enterprise': Falcon Guardian brings runtime protection to OpenAI Codex agents (visibility into agent activity, detection of compromised or unauthorized behavior, runtime control enforcement), and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Cyber powers CrowdStrike's FAIRR service with advanced cyber reasoning.
items.title: CrowdStrike brings Falcon to the OpenAI Marketplace; Falcon Guardian protects Codex agents at runtime
items.why_it_matters: Removes procurement friction for AI-heavy shops: 'spend your OpenAI commit on security' is a new buying path worth surfacing in accounts. For agent-security conversations, Falcon Guardian gives a concrete runtime-protection story — and GPT-5.6 Cyber inside FAIRR is competitive ammo in SIEM/SOC modernization bake-offs.

items.summary: Palo Alto Networks is expanding its NVIDIA collaboration around NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform reference design: Prisma AIRS AI Gateway will run on NVIDIA Vera CPUs (described as part of a future architecture) to centrally manage how agents connect to models and tools — inspecting interactions, restricting tool access, scrubbing sensitive data, tracking usage and cost. Prisma AIRS AI Runtime Security will run on NVIDIA BlueField DPUs for policy enforcement, integrated with DOCA Argus, Cortex XSIAM, OpenShell, and Idira for monitoring, response, and identity management.
items.title: Palo Alto Networks deepens NVIDIA partnership: AI-agent runtime security on Vera CPUs and BlueField DPUs
items.why_it_matters: AI-agent runtime security is becoming a real budget line, and PANW is planting the flag at the infrastructure layer — GPU/DPU-enforced policy. In network and security conversations, expect 'how do we govern what agents can touch?' to show up in RFPs; the BlueField/DPU angle lets PANW talk to datacenter teams, not just SOC buyers.

items.summary: Google Cloud launched AI-powered security agents natively in its infrastructure with Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Mandiant: PANW built an agent that plugs into Vertex AI to analyze application behavior across VMs, containers, and serverless, automatically isolating suspicious resources while feeding forensic detail to security teams, alongside Google Cloud Armor integration for traffic filtering. The agents monitor workloads, detect anomalies, and respond with minimal customer configuration.
items.title: Google Cloud ships AI security agents with Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Mandiant
items.why_it_matters: Cloud-embedded security agents are a new attach motion: minimal-config protection baked into the compute/storage/network layers. For GCP accounts, this is a joint-solution angle; for others, it's proof the 'security inside the cloud, not at the perimeter' shift is accelerating.

items.summary: Nutanix announced it was recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Distributed Hybrid Infrastructure, for both Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision. The release also notes expanded external-storage support: general availability for Dell PowerStore, updates for Everpure FlashArray and Dell PowerFlex, and limited availability for NetApp ONTAP — plus NKP Metal bare-metal Kubernetes, new agentic-AI capabilities, and sovereign/regulated deployment options.
items.title: Nutanix named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Distributed Hybrid Infrastructure
items.why_it_matters: Third-party validation to drop into VMware-vs-Nutanix conversations alongside the execution-over-vision story. The external-storage GA list is the sharper presales point: Nutanix no longer requires its own storage — customers can reuse PowerStore or FlashArray, which kills a common objection in HCI migrations.

items.summary: Zscaler's ThreatLabz 2026 Ransomware Report: ransomware data theft rose more than 275% year over year to 896.2 TB exfiltrated; blockchain transactions tied to ransomware payments hit $328 million; the average ransom payment rose 5.3% to $431,995. Manager-level titles and above made up 62% of victims, and attackers increasingly abuse trusted workplace tools including Microsoft Teams for data theft and lateral movement.
items.title: Zscaler ThreatLabz 2026 Ransomware Report: AI-driven ransomware, 275% jump in data theft, execs targeted
items.why_it_matters: Fresh, quotable stats for security discovery: exfiltration-not-encryption is the dominant ransomware model, execs are the target set, and trusted collaboration tools are the vector. Good opener for zero-trust and data-security conversations — ask how they'd spot 900 TB walking out through Teams.

items.summary: Cisco's Relentless Defense Report (survey of 8,000 security practitioners in 30 markets) finds only 8% of organizations qualify as top-tier defenders; just 21% can switch on a new security control within six months of budget approval; 40% of teams spend more time collecting and correlating data from disparate systems than chasing threats; and internal friction — procurement delays, data silos, unclear decision rights — is now the biggest drag on defense, weighted above tooling gaps. AI-era threats demand coordination no siloed team can deliver.
items.title: Cisco Relentless Defense Report: only 8% of orgs defend well; internal friction is the top blocker
items.why_it_matters: The buyer's problem is org friction, not missing tools — which is a services story. The 6-month control-deployment stat and the '8% relentless defenders' framing are strong opens for professional-services and platform-consolidation conversations. Also a clean segue into XDR/value-prop talks: teams drowning in data correlation want one pane.

items.summary: At Dell Technologies Forum 2026, Dell unveiled its latest AI commercial portfolio: Dell Pro 3, Pro 5, and Pro 7 AI PCs, Dell Pro Precision workstations, plus new displays and peripherals — pitched as bringing AI capabilities into the flow of work with security built in as a foundation. Dell also launched uDaan, an India skilling program targeting 23,000 young people for AI, cloud, and electronics-manufacturing careers.
items.title: Dell launches Dell Pro 3/5/7 AI PCs and Pro Precision workstations at Technologies Forum 2026
items.why_it_matters: New SKUs for client-refresh conversations: the AI PC refresh cycle is still the biggest near-term client opportunity, and Dell is leading with 'security as foundation' messaging — useful against vendors pitching AI PCs as a commodity spec play.

items.summary: VMware's Cloud Foundation blog details VCF 9.1 VKS (VMware Kubernetes Service) cluster-management improvements: lower cluster overhead, secure-by-default pod security contexts (CIS-benchmarked out of the box — a direct ask from regulated-industry customers), and policy-insight consolidation moved from in-cluster agents to the VKSM backend for better fleet-scale performance. VCF 9.1 is available now from the Broadcom Support Portal.
items.title: VCF 9.1 available: VKS cluster management gets leaner, secure-by-default, backend policy insights
items.why_it_matters: Broadcom keeps tightening the Kubernetes-on-VCF story, which matters for private-AI conversations: 'secure by default, CIS-benchmarked' is the compliance talking point for regulated shops running containers on VCF. Watch for vSphere Standard refresh details expected at VMware Explore Frankfurt.

items.title: Security advisory bundle AV26-966 covers SCG, ThinOS 10, Trusted Device Client, Rugged Control Center
items.summary: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security published alert AV26-966 on Sept 28 covering four Dell security updates: DSA-2026-410 (Rugged Control Center before 5.2.206), DSA-2026-385 (Secure Connect Gateway Policy Manager before 5.36.00.16), DSA-2026-404 (ThinOS 10), and DSA-2026-408 (Trusted Device Client before 8.1.359.0). Secure Connect Gateway and ThinOS sit in a lot of installed bases.
items.why_it_matters: Cheap, credible discovery fodder: ask installed-base accounts whether they're current on Secure Connect Gateway and ThinOS patches. SCG hygiene questions open security-services conversations.

items.title: Axis cameras now manageable through Meraki Dashboard via Cisco Cloud Control
items.summary: Axis devices can now be managed in the Cisco Meraki Dashboard through Cisco Cloud Control, with an Essentials tier (device health/visibility) and an Advantage tier (video analytics, 30-day cloud storage). Physical-security cameras ride the same management and licensing model as the network.
items.why_it_matters: Cross-sell wedge: accounts with Meraki networks plus Axis cameras can consolidate physical security under one dashboard. Modest story, but it gives Meraki-heavy shops a reason to talk camera refresh.

items.title: Broadcom deauthorizes Insight Enterprises, a top-tier VMware Pinnacle partner, in North America
items.summary: Broadcom has deauthorized Insight Enterprises from reselling VMware licenses and Broadcom-funded VCF Entitlement Services in North America. Insight finishes booked work through Oct 31, 2026. Partner executives say WWT and AHEAD are positioned to absorb the share, and some warn Broadcom is punishing partners that recommend competitive alternatives. (Publication date not shown on the page; fresh in the search index, so treat as late-September.)
items.why_it_matters: Another channel-ecosystem shock from Broadcom, and it feeds the VMware-replacement narrative directly. Expect this in every VMware renewal or Nutanix displacement conversation this week.

items.title: Launches Open Agent Safety Platform with 100+ partners, including CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks
items.summary: On Sept 28 NVIDIA announced the Open Agent Safety Platform: OpenShell (open-source agent sandbox runtime) plus Sentry (out-of-band enforcement on BlueField-4 DPUs) to contain 'agent drift', with 100+ organizations including CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks collaborating.
items.why_it_matters: This is the industry's emerging trust-layer framing for agentic AI. Customers evaluating 'security for AI agents' will hear CrowdStrike's and Palo Alto's pitches against this open framework — know both positions before the customer asks.

items.title: Acquires Ryax Technologies (French AI compute orchestration)
items.summary: Nutanix acquired Ryax, whose GPU-utilization and smart-scheduling technology will be integrated into the Nutanix Kubernetes Platform and Nutanix Enterprise AI to place agentic-AI workloads on the most cost-effective hardware across private data centers, hyperscalers, and neoclouds. (Announcement appears to be ~Sept 26; article dated Sept 28.)
items.why_it_matters: Nutanix is arming its Enterprise AI story with GPU-efficiency tooling — a direct competitive datapoint against VMware's AI Factory pitch in AI-infra deals.

items.title: "Agent Resilience" extends backup/rollback to AI agent infrastructure
items.summary: Cohesity's Agent Resilience discovers, protects (immutable snapshots), and recovers AI agent memory and configuration plus the data systems agents act on. Launch support for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore/Agents; select customers now, GA targeted end of 2026. (Launched at Cohesity Catalyst ~Sept 16; fresh analyst coverage Sept 28-29.)
items.why_it_matters: Direct counterpoint to Rubrik's agentic-cyber-resilience push below — expect 'who protects our AI agents' to be a discovery question this quarter.

items.title: Adds MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for agentic cyber resilience
items.summary: Rubrik MCP exposes the Rubrik Security Cloud API schema to customer AI agents so agents can run multi-step recovery and compliance workflows, with role-based access control and OWASP MCP Top 10-aligned guardrails. Private preview now, GA targeted October 2026; Rubrik AI is already used by roughly one-third of customers. (Dateline 'September 2026'; exact announcement date not pinned down.)
items.why_it_matters: Head-to-head with Cohesity's Agent Resilience: 'agentic cyber resilience' is the competitive front in backup/security this week. Know both roadmaps.

items.title: Announces intent to acquire PEAK:AIO (next-gen metadata architecture for AI infrastructure)
items.summary: NetApp will acquire UK-based PEAK:AIO, whose next-gen metadata architecture and high-performance parallel file system disaggregate metadata from data so shared storage scales alongside GPU clusters (trillions of files, exabyte-scale). The plan is to combine it with ONTAP while preserving ONTAP's resilience, security, and operational maturity. Also: NetApp INSIGHT 2026 runs Sept 29-Oct 1 in Las Vegas — watch for product announcements today/tomorrow.
items.why_it_matters: Metadata scaling is the key technical differentiator to use in AI-infra storage conversations. And with INSIGHT starting today, brief yourself on announcements before the customer does.

items.title: Two NetScaler zero-days (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772) under active exploitation; CISA adds both to KEV with Sept 30 remediation deadline
items.summary: Citrix disclosed eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws on Sept 27 via bulletin CTX697096 and confirmed that CVE-2026-88771 (input validation RCE, no special config needed) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory-buffer flaw leading to RCE/DoS, DTLS enabled by default on VPN virtual servers) were exploited as zero-days before patches existed. Both score CVSS 9.5. CISA added both to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Sept 27 and set a Sept 30 remediation due date for federal agencies. Fixed builds are 14.1-73.37 and 13.1-64.23. Patching alone is not enough: attackers deployed webshells and anti-forensics before the advisory, so Citrix advises checking for compromise before updating.
items.why_it_matters: NetScaler Gateway is the remote-access front door at many enterprise accounts, and this was a true zero-day window — exposed boxes had nothing to install for at least two days. This is an immediate outreach trigger: ask customers to confirm patch level (14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23) AND run forensic checks for webshells, since the fix does not evict an existing foothold. Also a positioning moment for zero-trust edge and managed detection conversations.

items.title: Operation Master exploited GlobalProtect auth bypass CVE-2026-0257 to seed a 2.4M-message invoice fraud campaign
items.summary: A fraud operation tracked as Operation Master used CVE-2026-0257, a Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect authentication bypass (originally rated CVSS 4.7, raised to 7.8 after exploitation was confirmed), to establish VPN sessions without valid credentials on seven gateways across four countries. From that foothold the group stole debtor records and sent 2.4 million fraudulent emails plus 1.4 million SMS. Rapid7 observed large-scale exploitation within four days of disclosure, and CISA added the CVE to its KEV catalog in May. Palo Alto Networks confirmed exploitation attempts against unpatched devices.
items.why_it_matters: The CVE itself is older, but this is fresh reporting on a major real-world campaign it enabled — strong call-prep material for GlobalProtect accounts: the four-day gap between disclosure and mass exploitation is a concrete argument for aggressive patch cadence on edge VPN appliances. Also worth checking that any auth-override cookie configurations in customer GlobalProtect deployments match the advisory's mitigation guidance.

items.title: NVIDIA launches Open Agent Safety Platform (OpenShell + Sentry) with 100+ partners including Cisco, CrowdStrike, Dell, HPE, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Fortinet
items.summary: NVIDIA announced the Open Agent Safety Platform on Sept 28: an open software platform and reference system design for securing AI agents from testing through deployment, with full-stack governance across the software, hardware/compute, and robotics layers that run agents. It includes OpenShell and Sentry components, the latter able to quarantine agents that move outside their boundaries in milliseconds. Named partners include Anthropic, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, HPE, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, Red Hat, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Zscaler, and the U.S. Department of Defense.
items.why_it_matters: Agentic AI security is becoming a datacenter architecture conversation, not just an app-layer one — customers running agent pilots now have to answer how agents are governed at the infrastructure layer. Nearly every vendor on your coverage list is on the partner wall, which makes this a clean discovery question for security and AI-infrastructure conversations: who owns runtime agent controls at your accounts, and is it a platform or a patchwork?

items.title: NetApp announces intent to acquire PEAK:AIO to scale AI storage
items.summary: NetApp said September 25 it plans to acquire PEAK:AIO, a small storage-software firm focused on metadata services and parallel file-system technology for AI infrastructure. The goal is to bring PEAK:AIO's approach — which separates metadata handling from data storage so metadata can scale independently — into ONTAP, reducing GPU stalls as clusters and file counts grow. PEAK:AIO's pNFS Lattice project is an open-source, scale-out metadata server for NFSv4.2 developed with Los Alamos National Laboratory. Terms were not disclosed.
items.why_it_matters: Gives you a fresh AI-infrastructure talking point on NetApp calls: ONTAP is getting a real answer to the metadata-scale bottleneck in AI training clusters. Watch for customers asking how this competes with Weka/VAST/Lustre-style parallel file systems, and expect NetApp to pitch existing ONTAP shops an 'evolution path' rather than a rip-and-replace.

items.title: Actively exploited Cisco Secure Email Gateway SQL injection (CVE-2026-76461); hardening release fixes four more CVEs
items.summary: Cisco disclosed September 15 that CVE-2026-76461, an SQL injection flaw in Secure Email Gateway, is under active exploitation, and published indicators of compromise so customers can check whether their gateways were already hit. The same fixed AsyncOS releases (15.5.5-014, 16.0.4-302, 16.5.0-780) also remediate four companion vulnerabilities found in an internal review: CVE-2026-76440, CVE-2026-76441, CVE-2026-20353, and CVE-2026-76443. There is no workaround for the exploited flaw. Cloud SEG appliances were patched by Cisco; on-prem physical and virtual appliances must upgrade, with Cisco recommending the 16.5 branch as the target. This follows a September 16 CVSS-10.0 authentication bypass in ISE (CVE-2026-76460), also confirmed exploited.
items.why_it_matters: Two actively exploited Cisco zero-days in two days (SEG + ISE) is a strong reason to proactively call security contacts, not wait for them. Lead with 'patch or re-image, don't patch in place if compromise is suspected' — Cisco's own guidance says re-image nodes where malicious activity is suspected. Good opening to talk email-security posture and ISE patch hygiene.

items.title: Neocloud GPU rents climbing again: Nebius raising selected Nvidia GPU tariffs 17-21% from October 1
items.summary: According to Reuters reporting covered this week, neocloud provider Nebius will raise rental tariffs for selected Nvidia GPUs by 17 to 21 percent starting October 1 — its second increase in three months. The move signals that demand for GPU capacity continues to outpace supply and that end-customer willingness to pay remains strong. Separately, Nvidia rolled out its DSX Ready program (binding requirements for battery storage and cooling in its AI-factory reference designs) and Isaac ROS 5.0 for physical AI.
items.why_it_matters: Useful economics ammo for AI-infrastructure conversations: public/neocloud GPU pricing keeps rising, which strengthens the TCO case for customer-owned GPU infrastructure (and the platforms — VCF, Nutanix, Dell, HPE — that run it). If a customer is pricing AI workloads in the cloud, this is a data point for the repatriation talk.
